title: AI Visibility Tools 2026: 12 Compared. Where Each One Wins.
summary: Compare 12 AI visibility tools for 2026 by execution, engine coverage, SEO depth, data, customer evidence, and price.
body_markdown:
In 2026 the real choice isn't which dashboard to buy. Every serious tool tracks the same engines. The choice is how far you want the product to carry the work.Profound is the most established analytics product and now has a real closed loop through Projects and Aim.Writesonic tracks the same engines and runs autonomous agents that do content, outreach, and technical work.Ahrefs Brand Radar is the widest research index for market mapping.


**Disclosure:** I'm Samanyou Garg, founder and CEO of Writesonic, one of the 12 tools here. I scored every product on the same six criteria and published each criterion score below so you can check my work. Pricing verified July 30, 2026.


## Key takeaways


- **Tracking is a commodity.** All 12 tools report mentions, citations, sentiment, and share of voice across the major answer engines. Engine coverage differs at the edges, and those differences are shrinking.
- **Execution is what separates them.** Ask any vendor what happens after the dashboard shows a gap.Writesonic scores highest on execution because its autonomous agents carry a gap through content, outreach, and technical fixes, then measure what moved.
- **Compare the action loops.** ChooseProfound for established analytics plus the newer Projects and Aim workflow. ChooseWritesonic when you need deeper autonomous execution across content, outreach, and technical work.
- **Enterprises and agencies both have options.** Nearly every tool here, Writesonic included, handles multiple brands, projects, and large teams. Treat multi-project support as a baseline, not a differentiator.
- **Most AI citations come from other people's sites.**[Muck Rack's May 2026 study](https://muckrack.com/blog/what-is-ai-reading-may-2026) of more than 25 million cited links found 84% came from earned media. Whatever you buy, on-site work alone won't get you recommended.


## The 12 AI visibility tools at a glance

## What GEO and AEO actually mean


**SEO** is how your pages rank in traditional search results. **GEO** and **AEO** are two names for the same job: making sure answer engines find, understand, cite, and recommend your brand inside generated answers. Teams need both, because AI answers still pull heavily from searchable web sources.


## What matters before you choose a tool


Third-party coverage shapes a large share of AI citations, which is also what our own[study of what drives AI visibility growth](https://writesonic.com/blog/what-drives-ai-visibility-growth-study) found.[Muck Rack's May 2026 study](https://muckrack.com/blog/what-is-ai-reading-may-2026) analyzed more than 25 million cited links across ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.


The study found that earned media accounts for 84% of all AI citations. As Muck Rack cofounder and CEO Greg Galant put it, "For communications teams, that is validation that the work they do to earn coverage in the right outlets has real consequences beyond traditional metrics."


Price also needs context. Entry plans often limit engines, prompts, refresh rates, shopping data, or execution. Profound and Semrush require annual billing for their advertised $99 entry prices. Check how many actions, engines, and prompts each plan actually includes.


Monitoring and execution now overlap. Several products recommend content or technical work. Fewer carry that work through approval, delivery, and later measurement.


## How I evaluated these AI visibility tools


I used six weighted criteria:


1. **Execution, 25%.** How far the product carries work from detection through prioritization, remediation, approval, delivery, and measurement.
2. **AI platform coverage, 20%.** Which answer engines are supported, including differences in geography, model, interface, and refresh cadence.
3. **SEO and AI visibility depth, 15%.** Technical SEO, content, links, demand, crawlability, and their connection to generated answers.
4. **Data scale and freshness, 15%.** Response coverage, historical depth, update frequency, locations, and modeled-demand limits.
5. **Customer evidence, 15%.** Named case studies and documented outcomes scored above testimonials or logo walls.
6. **Self-serve to enterprise fit, 10%.** Entry price, trials, seats, exports, APIs, SSO, security, and governance, so a small team and a large one can both tell whether the product suits them.


Each criterion receives a score from 1 to 5. A score of 1 means absent or very limited. A score of 3 means capable with meaningful constraints. A score of 5 means category-leading.


I calculated each total by multiplying every criterion score by its published weight. Features available on widely sold plans count for more than features that appear only in custom contracts.


Vendor scale claims aren't directly comparable. Prompts, conversations, responses, citations, and modeled searches measure different things. I treated each as evidence within its stated unit.


## 1. Profound: best for established analytics and a new action loop, from $99 per month


Profound is the most established product in this category. Its polished interface covers prompt research, citations, sentiment, competitors, shopping results, and traffic from automated agents.


It also ships Agents, Sheets, Projects, and Aim. Projects turns findings into ranked tasks, while Aim converts signals into work and measures what moved. That closed loop shipped in late June and early July 2026.[Fortune reported on February 24, 2026](https://fortune.com/2026/02/24/exclusive-as-ai-threatens-search-profound-raises-96-million-to-help-brands-stay-visible/) that Profound raised a $96 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $155 million.


**Best for:** Teams that want established analytics, polished reporting, and a new action loop backed by Projects and Aim.


**Key features:**


- Researches conversations and prompts
- Analyzes citations, sentiment, competitors, and answer details
- Turns findings into ranked work through Projects
- Runs ongoing prioritization and measurement through Aim
- Adds shopping, merchant, and paid visibility analysis on qualifying plans


**Pricing:**


- Starter costs $99 per month, billed annually.
- Growth costs $399 per month, billed annually.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.
- Profound doesn't publish clear trial terms.


**Pros:**


- Its interface makes complex answer data easier to analyze and report.
- Projects and Aim create a real path from findings to managed work and measurement.
- Higher plans provide broad engine coverage and detailed shopping analysis.


**Cons:**


- Projects and Aim are new, so their maturity remains the fair execution concern.
- Agent runs draw on monthly credits that cap the work available on each plan.
- Starter tracks ChatGPT only, while broader engines and shopping sit on higher tiers.


**Choose it when:** You want established analytics and can work within a newer action system, plan-level agent credits, and tiered engine coverage.


## 2. Writesonic: best for execution depth, from $99 per month


Writesonic tracks answer engines at comparable depth, then uses autonomous marketing agents to act on what it finds. The agents combine AI visibility and SEO data, produce or fix content, pursue off-page mentions, apply approved technical changes, and measure what moved.


Playbooks store repeatable workflows, Grids support bulk analysis, and the task system coordinates work. AI ad visibility and shopping results sit in the same product.


**Best for:** Enterprise and agency teams that need autonomous agents to carry visibility gaps through content, outreach, and technical work.


**Key features:**


- Tracks ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and more
- Combines AI visibility data with SEO data
- Runs autonomous agents for content, outreach, and technical fixes
- Supports repeatable and bulk work through Playbooks, Grids, and tasks
- Measures results after approved changes ship


**Pricing:**


- Starter costs $99 monthly or $79 per month annually.
- Basic costs $249 monthly or $199 per month annually.
- Growth costs $499 monthly or $399 per month annually.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.
- The seven-day trial requires no card.


**Rating:**[G2 listed Writesonic at 4.7 out of 5 across about 2,214 reviews in July 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/writesonic/reviews) .


**Pros:**


- Autonomous agents complete content, outreach, and technical work instead of stopping at recommendations.
- AI ad visibility and shopping results sit inside the same system.
- Multi-brand support, multiple projects, SSO, and security controls support larger teams.


**Cons:**


- The wider system takes more time to learn in the first week than a focused tracker.
- The number of agent actions available each month depends on the plan.


**Choose it when:** Your backlog is growing faster than your team can complete the content, outreach, and technical work.


## 3. Ahrefs Brand Radar: best for one-off market research, from $199 per month


Ahrefs Brand Radar works like an extension of Ahrefs' keyword explorer pointed at AI answers. Its prebuilt indexes let teams research brands, domains, citations, topics, and competitors before deciding which prompts deserve regular tracking.


That makes it useful for a one-off market-mapping exercise. It's weaker for day-to-day monitoring, and it reports what it finds without acting on it.


**Best for:** Existing Ahrefs customers running a market-mapping exercise before creating a smaller daily monitoring program elsewhere.


**Key features:**


- Searches large prebuilt AI answer indexes
- Researches brands, domains, citations, topics, and competitors
- Reports mentions, estimated impressions, and share of voice
- Connects findings to search demand and web visibility
- Adds context from Reddit, YouTube, and TikTok data


**Pricing:**


- Individual AI indexes start at $199 per month.
- The all-index bundle costs $699 per month.
- Custom prompt packages start at $50 per month.


**Rating:**[G2 showed a 4.5 out of 5 rating across about 710 reviews in July 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/ahrefs/reviews) .


**Pros:**


- Prebuilt indexes let teams map a market before defining every prompt.
- Unlimited brand and domain research supports broad exploration.
- Ahrefs connects AI answer research with familiar search-demand and web-visibility data.


**Cons:**


- Core chatbot indexes refresh monthly, which limits day-to-day monitoring.
- Brand Radar researches and reports but doesn't act on its findings.
- Estimated impressions use Google search demand as a model, and costs rise when teams combine indexes.


**Choose it when:** You need to understand the market before committing to a fixed prompt set and daily monitoring tool.


## 4. Peec AI: best for affordable tracking for smaller teams, from $95 per month


Peec AI is a tracking-focused product, and it does that job well at a lower price. It tracks major answer engines on daily or weekly schedules, covers shopping visibility, and provides prioritized actions.


Every paid plan includes unlimited seats.[TechCrunch reported on November 17, 2025](https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/17/as-consumers-ditch-google-for-chatgpt-peec-ai-raises-21m-to-help-brands-adapt/) that Peec AI raised a $21 million Series A and, based on company disclosures, had more than $4 million in annual recurring revenue and 1,300 customers at the time.


**Best for:** SMBs and teams starting AI visibility work that want affordable tracking without per-seat charges.


**Key features:**


- Tracks prompts on daily or weekly schedules
- Reports mentions, citations, and competitor movement
- Supports multiple projects and unlimited seats
- Analyzes shopping visibility across several engines
- Prioritizes page, editorial, reference-site, and user-generated-content work


**Pricing:**


- Starter costs $95 per month.
- Pro costs $245 per month.
- Advanced costs $495 per month.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.
- A seven-day trial is available, although Peec doesn't state current card requirements.


**Rating:**[G2 showed 4.9 out of 5 across only 12 reviews in July 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/peec-ai/reviews) .


**Pros:**


- The $95 entry price suits smaller teams starting with tracking.
- Every paid plan includes unlimited seats.
- Daily or weekly schedules let teams choose how often they monitor prompts.


**Cons:**


- Self-serve plans include three selected models, and adding another model costs extra.
- Peec Actions prioritizes work, but teams still complete the final execution.
- The G2 score comes from a thin base of 12 reviews.


**Choose it when:** You need affordable tracking now and can complete the resulting work elsewhere.


## 5. Searchable: best for small and mid-sized European teams, from $125 per month


Searchable has gained traction with small and mid-sized European teams. Its founding team also has a large LinkedIn following, which gives the company unusual visibility with buyers in that market.


The product reports individual SKUs, prices, ratings, merchants, categories, platforms, and appearance counts. It can also research prompts, prepare plans, draft content briefs, suggest schema, and assign technical tasks.[PR Newswire reported on May 18, 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/searchable-secures-14m-from-headline-at-85m-valuation-as-ai-reshapes-how-customers-are-searching-and-buying-302774547.html) that Searchable raised $14 million in a round led by Headline at an $85 million valuation.


**Best for:** Small and mid-sized European teams that want a self-serve visibility product with product and merchant reporting.


**Key features:**


- Reports individual SKUs, prices, ratings, and merchants
- Analyzes categories, platforms, and appearance counts
- Shows which retailers appear in product carousels
- Supports prompt research, planning, and content briefs
- Suggests schema and assigns technical tasks


**Pricing:**


- Pro costs $125 per month.
- Scale costs $400 per month.
- Enterprise costs $999 per month.
- Further controls use custom pricing.
- The 14-day trial doesn't require a card.


**Pros:**


- Its self-serve entry price and no-card trial suit smaller and mid-sized European teams.
- Product Gallery separates brand, product, and merchant visibility.
- Planning, content briefs, schema suggestions, and technical tasks extend the product beyond reporting.


**Cons:**


- The pricing FAQ and comparison table conflict on engine availability.
- Engine coverage varies by plan.
- Public documentation doesn't show direct CMS publishing, author outreach, or Reddit execution.


**Choose it when:** You're a small or mid-sized European team that wants self-serve tracking with product and merchant detail.


## 6. Scrunch AI: best for agent-facing content delivery, from $250 per month


Scrunch is now part of Sitecore. Its Agent Experience Platform, or AXP, can serve approved site content in a format designed for automated agents.


This is execution at the delivery layer, which makes Scrunch especially relevant to Sitecore customers and enterprise DXP teams.[Sitecore announced the acquisition on June 3, 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/sitecore-acquires-scrunch-to-help-brands-influence-discovery-and-buying-decisions-in-the-ai-search-era-302790214.html) , saying Scrunch served more than 500 brands and agencies.[Bloomberg reportedly placed the transaction near $225 million](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-18/sitecore-said-to-acquire-scrunch-for-225-million) , although neither company confirmed that price.


**Best for:** Sitecore and enterprise DXP teams deciding how approved content reaches automated agents.


**Key features:**


- Monitors answers across major engines
- Analyzes citations and pages
- Manages prompts
- Reports traffic from automated agents
- Delivers agent-facing content through AXP


**Pricing:**


- Core costs $250 per month and covers 125 prompts.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.
- The seven-day trial doesn't require a card.


**Pros:**


- AXP addresses how approved content reaches automated agents.
- Sitecore ownership makes the product relevant to teams already using that DXP.
- Monitoring, traffic reporting, and delivery sit in the same system.


**Cons:**


- AXP remains in limited availability.
- Core covers a narrower set of engines, so full coverage means Enterprise.
- It can require more technical involvement than a conventional visibility dashboard.
- Its value depends on whether agent-facing delivery is an infrastructure priority.


**Choose it when:** Your visibility problem sits inside the DXP and delivery stack, especially if Sitecore already runs it.


## 7. Conductor: best for enterprise SEO governance, with custom pricing


Conductor fits large SEO organizations that need AI visibility inside an established governance and reporting system. It separates model-training crawlers, live-search bots, and user-triggered fetches.


The product connects prompt groups and answer data with technical SEO and content work.[GlobeNewswire reported on November 16, 2021](https://www.globenewswire.com/ph/news-release/2021/11/16/2335248/0/en/Conductor-Raises-150M-in-Funding-to-Power-the-Company-s-Next-Phase-of-Growth-in-the-Organic-Marketing-Revolution.html) that Conductor raised $150 million from Bregal Sagemount.


**Best for:** Large SEO organizations with established procurement, permission, governance, and reporting requirements.


**Key features:**


- Covers a broad set of answer engines
- Groups prompts and provides response APIs
- Separates model-training, live-search, and user-triggered crawlers
- Monitors technical SEO issues
- Connects answer data with content planning


**Pricing:**


- Conductor uses custom enterprise pricing.
- A three-week no-card trial is available, but purchasing goes through sales.


**Pros:**


- AI visibility sits inside an established enterprise SEO system.
- Crawler-type analysis distinguishes different automated access patterns.
- Enterprise permissions and reporting support large organizations.


**Cons:**


- Essentials includes no AI Search credits, and AI visibility starts on Growth.
- Conductor detects technical issues but doesn't claim to apply every fix.
- It lacks dedicated shopping and paid-placement analytics.


**Choose it when:** Enterprise SEO governance matters more than self-serve pricing or a standalone execution system.


## 8. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit: best for existing Semrush and Adobe teams, from $99 per month


Semrush is most useful when a team already relies on its search suite or Adobe's enterprise products. The toolkit covers brand mentions, topics, citations, sentiment, estimated AI traffic, and custom prompt tracking.


Adobe customers get another path through Adobe Brand Visibility and Adobe Experience Manager. Semrush reported $376.8 million in fiscal 2024 revenue and $411.6 million in annual recurring revenue in its[April 2025 SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1831840/000162828025018235/semr-20250417.htm) .


**Best for:** Organizations already using Semrush for search work or Adobe for enterprise content delivery.


**Key features:**


- Reports brand mentions, topics, citations, and sentiment
- Estimates AI traffic
- Tracks custom prompt positions
- Connects findings to wider Semrush search data
- Supports eligible Adobe customers through Adobe Brand Visibility and AEM


**Pricing:**


- The entry toolkit costs $99 per month for one domain and 25 daily tracked prompts, billed annually.
- Extra domains cost $99 per month.
- Fifty additional prompts cost about $60 per month.
- Semrush One Advanced costs $549 per month.
- A seven-day trial is available.


**Pros:**


- Existing Semrush users can keep AI visibility beside their wider search data.
- Eligible Adobe customers have a path from reporting into AEM-based delivery.
- The entry toolkit provides self-serve access for one domain and daily prompt tracking.


**Cons:**


- Self-serve mention analysis covers more surfaces than custom position tracking.
- AI Shopping requires Enterprise AIO.
- There is no self-serve shopping module or paid AI-placement tracking.


**Choose it when:** Keeping AI visibility inside your current Semrush or Adobe system matters more than buying a separate product.


## 9. Otterly.AI: best for a low-cost tracking start, from $29 per month


Otterly.AI has the lowest ongoing paid entry price here. It's a tracking-focused tool that suits SMBs and teams running their first AI visibility program.


The product monitors brand mentions, citations, sentiment, ads, and shopping cards. Recent additions include citation-change reporting, query fan-out analysis, PDF exports, an API, and an MCP server.


**Best for:** SMBs and teams getting started that want affordable monitoring and downloadable reports.


**Key features:**


- Monitors brand mentions, citations, and sentiment
- Detects ChatGPT ads and shopping cards
- Tracks ads within Google AI Overviews
- Reports citation changes and query fan-out
- Provides PDF exports, an API, and an MCP server


**Pricing:**


- Lite costs $29 per month.
- Standard costs $189 per month.
- Premium costs $489 per month.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.
- The seven-day trial doesn't require a card.


**Rating:**[G2 listed Otterly.AI at 4.8 out of 5 across 42 reviews in July 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/otterlyai/pricing) .


**Pros:**


- It has the lowest ongoing paid entry price here.
- Citation-change and query fan-out reports help explain visibility movement.
- Exports and data connections make monitoring results available outside the dashboard.


**Cons:**


- Google AI Mode, Gemini, and Claude cost extra.
- Ads and shopping features report appearances but don't manage campaigns, catalogs, or individual SKUs.
- Execution support is thinner than in products built to complete the resulting work.


**Choose it when:** You need dependable, low-cost tracking and can run the resulting work elsewhere.


## 10. AthenaHQ: best for free multi-engine sampling, then $295 per month


AthenaHQ offers a free Essential allocation that lets teams sample several engines. Its paid product adds on-page and off-page actions, citation analysis, crawler-access management, content work, and publishing connections such as Shopify.


[FinSMEs reported on June 18, 2025](https://www.finsmes.com/2025/06/athena-raises-2-2m-in-seed-funding.html) that AthenaHQ raised $2.2 million from Y Combinator and other investors. FinSMEs also reported a catalog of more than 3 million AI responses at that time.


**Best for:** Teams that want to sample several engines before testing a paid action workflow.


**Key features:**


- Samples several engines through the free Essential allocation
- Analyzes citations
- Manages crawler access
- Supports on-page, off-page, and content actions
- Connects to publishing systems such as Shopify


**Pricing:**


- Essential includes 300 free credits.
- Starter costs $295 per month.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.


**Rating:**[G2 showed 4.9 out of 5 across 34 reviews in July 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/athenahq/reviews) .


**Pros:**


- The free allocation provides a useful multi-engine evaluation.
- The paid product covers both analysis and action workflows.
- GA4, API, and MCP connections are available on paid plans.


**Cons:**


- There is no permanent paid tier between the free sampler and $295 per month.
- API access and extra credits can add cost.
- Ecommerce support doesn't include detailed SKU visibility, merchant share, or paid-placement tracking.


**Choose it when:** You want a meaningful free evaluation and can tolerate the jump to the first paid plan.


## 11. SE Visible: best for simple tracking with unlimited seats, from $99 per month


SE Visible is a straightforward tracker covering ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Perplexity. It reports mentions, citations, sentiment, and competitor comparisons.


Every plan includes unlimited users. Existing SE Ranking customers can also add AI Search to the wider SEO product.


**Best for:** Teams that want simple AI monitoring without per-seat charges.


**Key features:**


- Tracks five named answer surfaces
- Reports brand mentions and citations
- Analyzes sentiment and competitor comparisons
- Supports multiple countries and languages
- Connects to the wider SE Ranking suite for existing customers


**Pricing:**


- Basic costs $99 per month.
- Core costs $189 per month.
- Plus costs $355 per month.
- Enterprise uses custom pricing.
- The ten-day trial requires a card.


**Pros:**


- Every plan includes unlimited users.
- Five-engine coverage provides a clear monitoring baseline.
- [G2 listed SE Ranking at 4.7 out of 5 across about 2,396 reviews in July 2026](https://www.g2.com/products/se-ranking/reviews) , although that rating covers the parent platform rather than SE Visible.


**Cons:**


- Standalone data refreshes weekly.
- Exports are CSV-only, while API and MCP access require the separate SE Ranking platform.
- SE Visible doesn't execute content, outreach, or technical fixes.


**Choose it when:** Many people need access and weekly monitoring is frequent enough.


## 12. HubSpot AEO: best for CRM-grounded prompt discovery, from $50 per month


HubSpot AEO works best when prompt and recommendation data can use CRM, campaign, and deal context already stored in HubSpot.


The standalone beta tracks ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise add CRM context and paths into HubSpot's content and social tools.[HubSpot's February 2026 investor filing](https://ir.hubspot.com/node/15361/html) reported $3.13 billion in fiscal 2025 revenue and 288,706 customers at year-end for the wider HubSpot business.


**Best for:** HubSpot customers who want basic AI visibility connected to their existing CRM and campaign data.


**Key features:**


- Discovers prompts using HubSpot context
- Monitors brand and competitor appearances
- Produces prioritized recommendations
- Adds CRM and campaign context on qualifying plans
- Connects recommendations to HubSpot content tools


**Pricing:**


- HubSpot AEO costs $50 per month or $45 per month annually.
- Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise include it.
- The current trial includes 25 free prompts across three supported engines and requires no card.


**Pros:**


- Prompt discovery can use context already stored in HubSpot.
- Marketing Hub customers can connect recommendations to existing content and social tools.
- The no-card sampler includes 25 prompts across three engines.


**Cons:**


- Coverage stops at ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity.
- Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Claude, and Copilot aren't included.
- Deeper execution depends on other Marketing Hub tools.


**Choose it when:** Your CRM and campaign context already lives in HubSpot and three-engine coverage is enough.


## Criterion-level scoring


Scores run 1 to 5. A 1 means absent or very limited, a 3 means capable with real constraints, a 5 means category-leading. The numbers are mine, but every one of them is visible here so you can disagree with a specific cell rather than the conclusion.


# Tool Execution 25% AI coverage 20% SEO + AI depth 15% Data scale 15% Customer evidence 15% Self-serve to enterprise fit 10% Weighted total


1 Profound 3 5 3 5 5 4 4.10


2 Writesonic 5 4 5 5 4 4 4.55


3 Ahrefs Brand Radar 2 5 5 5 5 2 3.95


4 Peec AI 3 4 3 5 4 5 3.85


5 Searchable 3 4 3 4 4 5 3.70


6 Scrunch AI 4 5 2 3 3 3 3.50


7 Conductor 2 5 5 3 4 1 3.40

Writesonic scores highest at 4.55, and the reason is execution. It's the only product here whose agents take a detected gap through content, outreach, and technical work and then measure what changed. On tracking itself, Writesonic and Profound are close.


I've still listed Profound first. Ranking my own product number one on my own site isn't a ranking anyone should trust, so I'd rather show you the criterion scores and let you do the arithmetic. Profound earns its place on analytics depth, engine breadth, the most polished interface in the category, and the strongest customer evidence. It's the most established and most talked-about product here.


Ahrefs Brand Radar scores 3.95 on research breadth and data scale. It loses ground on execution, because it reports and researches rather than acts, and on cost once you combine indexes.


Funding didn't affect any score. It signals market backing, and it isn't one of the six criteria.


## What I'd actually do


Most buyers facing a twelve-tool comparison evaluate the wrong axis. They compare engine counts and dashboard screenshots because both are easy to inspect during a trial. I wouldn't give either much weight. Engine coverage is close to a commodity now, and I expect it to converge further every quarter. The meaningful difference starts after the dashboard shows a gap.


I'd put two finalists through a fortnight-long test. I'd choose five prompts tied to revenue, run the same prompts through both products, and hold the engines, locations, and cadence constant. At the end, I'd compare what each tool produced: published content, completed outreach, approved technical fixes, or a prioritized task an owner could actually finish. I wouldn't judge the winner by how polished its charts looked on day one. A tool that shows you a problem you already knew about has sold you a mirror.


My conflict is obvious: I founded Writesonic, and Writesonic appears in this ranking. I'd pick it when I wanted one system to find gaps and carry content, outreach, and technical work through completion. But I wouldn't pretend it's the best buy for everyone. I'd buy Profound when executive reporting and established analytics mattered more than execution depth, especially if I already had a strong operating team. I'd buy Ahrefs Brand Radar for a one-off market-mapping project where broad research mattered more than daily action. For a small team that only needed affordable monitoring, I'd choose Otterly.AI and keep the extra budget for the work itself.


## Match the tool to your operating model


### Choose Writesonic when you need the number to move


Writesonic fits teams that don't have the headcount, or the patience, to turn findings into completed work. Its autonomous agents do the content, outreach, and technical work with approval, then measure what changed. If your problem is execution capacity rather than reporting, this is the one to trial.


Ask how many actions the plan includes each month and size that against the work in front of you.


### Choose Profound for established analytics and a newer action loop


Profound fits teams that want the category's best-known analytics product, a polished interface, and a real workflow through Projects and Aim. Its data scale, engine breadth, and customer evidence are genuinely strong.


Confirm when Projects and Aim became available in the quoted package, how agent credits map to your backlog, and which engines and shopping features the tier includes.


### Choose Ahrefs when exploration comes before tracking


Brand Radar works well when you don't yet know which prompts, competitors, publishers, or topics deserve daily monitoring. Its prebuilt indexes help define the category before you create a smaller tracked-prompt program.


Use it for the mapping exercise. Pair it with another product for day-to-day monitoring and action.


### Choose Peec AI when you want affordable tracking with seats included


Peec AI suits SMBs and teams just starting AI visibility work. Its $95 entry price, unlimited seats, and daily or weekly schedules make it a practical tracking product.


Actions prioritizes the work, but your team still needs to complete it.


### Choose SE Visible when simple weekly tracking and broad access matter


SE Visible includes unlimited users and covers five named answer surfaces. It suits teams that want a straightforward tracker and don't need daily refreshes or built-in execution.


### Choose Searchable when you're a small or mid-sized European team


Searchable has built traction among smaller European teams, helped by a founding team with a large LinkedIn following. Its self-serve product also provides individual product and merchant reporting alongside planning, briefs, schema suggestions, and technical tasks.


Confirm the exact engine list during the no-card trial because its public documents conflict.


### Choose Conductor or Semrush when replacing the SEO suite isn't practical


Conductor and Semrush reduce tool sprawl for existing customers. Conductor brings stronger enterprise SEO governance and technical monitoring. Semrush offers a lower entry price, while eligible Adobe customers can connect reporting to AEM-based delivery.


### Choose Otterly.AI or HubSpot AEO for a low initial spend


Otterly.AI has the lowest ongoing paid plan and suits SMBs starting with tracking. HubSpot AEO costs $50 monthly and may already be included in a Marketing Hub contract.


### Choose Scrunch AI when agent delivery is an infrastructure decision


Scrunch addresses how approved content reaches automated agents. That makes it relevant to DXP and platform teams, especially Sitecore customers. A marketing team seeking a quick tracker may find the required technical work disproportionate.


## How to compare your finalists


AI visibility scores are directional. Answers change across models, locations, interfaces, and repeated runs. Modeled demand adds another source of uncertainty.


Run the same five commercial prompts through each finalist. Ask every vendor to show:


- The source answer and citation history
- The engine, model, geography, and refresh schedule
- The plan limit attached to each feature
- The next recommended action and its concrete output
- How the product measures a completed action afterward


Keep the prompts and measurement window stable. This small test reveals more than another feature checklist.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is an AI visibility tool?


It tracks how answer engines mention, cite, describe, or recommend a brand. Most products monitor prompts, compare competitors, identify cited sources, and calculate share of voice. More advanced tools add shopping results, advertising appearances, technical diagnostics, content work, outreach support, or agent-facing delivery.


### How do AI visibility tools differ from SEO tools?


AI visibility tools analyze generated answers and the sources behind them. SEO tools focus mainly on search results, keywords, pages, links, and crawlability. The categories overlap because answer engines retrieve web pages and search results, but their reports, sampling methods, and recommended actions differ.


### Which AI engines should a visibility tool cover?


Start with the engines your customers actually use. For many teams, that includes ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Gemini, and Perplexity. Claude and Copilot can matter more for B2B research. Confirm the exact model, interface, location, and refresh cadence before comparing coverage claims.


### How much do AI visibility tools cost?


Paid products in this comparison start at $29 per month and extend to custom enterprise contracts. Many self-serve tools begin between $95 and $199 monthly. Extra engines, prompts, domains, locations, shopping data, APIs, and execution features can raise the real monthly cost substantially.


### Are there free AI visibility tools?


Free access exists, but it is limited. AthenaHQ offers a 300-credit sampler across several engines. HubSpot AEO currently includes 25 free prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity without requiring a card. Ahrefs and Semrush also provide limited checkers rather than complete ongoing monitoring plans.


### How often should I measure AI visibility?


Daily or weekly tracking fits high-value prompts, active launches, and fast-moving categories. Monthly analysis can be enough for broad discovery and executive reporting. Use the same prompts, engines, locations, and measurement window each time. Consistency matters more than buying the highest available refresh frequency.


## Choose the workflow before the vendor


Profound is the most established analytics product here and now has a real closed loop through Projects and Aim. Its fair constraints are the maturity of that workflow, per-plan agent credits, and tiered engine coverage. Writesonic scores highest when execution depth carries the most weight because its autonomous agents complete content, outreach, and technical work. Ahrefs Brand Radar wins when a one-off research exercise comes before daily prompt tracking.


Every other tool has a clearer fit. Searchable has traction with small and mid-sized European teams. Scrunch handles agent delivery. Peec AI and Otterly.AI give SMBs and teams getting started lower-cost tracking options.


Choose the operating model first. Then buy the plan containing the capability you will actually use.
